h1: AI for the robots you already have
lead: We do not build robots. We make the ones you own easier to use: a help bot that knows your manuals, orders in plain language that a human approves, and a short AI report on your whole fleet every morning.
bub: Put the 2 red boxes on pallet 2, please.
ofH: Four ways we add value to your robots
ofP: Start small with the help bot, then add more when it pays off. Everything runs on top of the robot's own controller and safety system.
o1p: Knows your manuals, fault codes and service notes. Technicians and customers ask in their own language and get the right steps, with the page it comes from.
o2p: Operators say what they need. The AI turns it into the robot's own commands, rules check it, a human approves. Less programming, faster changeovers.
o3p: Reads the logs your robots already make and writes a short morning report: what stopped, why it probably stopped, what to check first.
o4p: Do it yourself: step-by-step guides with prompts, safety checklists and test cases for each of the three above.
hP: A demo with a made-up robot, the "MX-1". Pick a fault code. A real help bot answers from your own manuals and says where the answer comes from. If it is not sure, it sends the question to a person.
fH: A morning report for the whole fleet
fP: The AI reads status and error logs from your robots and writes what matters, in a few lines. Demo data below.
dTag: Demo with made-up robots and numbers.
sP: Robots can hurt people and break things. This is how we keep the AI in its place.
s1: The AI never drives the motors
s1p: It only proposes commands through the robot's normal interface. The robot's certified safety system keeps the final say.
s2p: Every plan that moves something waits for a clear yes. Emergency stops always work and always win.
s3p: No-go zones, speed and payload limits are checked by fixed rules. Unsafe orders are refused, not "negotiated".
s4p: Each order, plan, approval and stop is written down, so you can see who decided what.
s5p: New tasks are tested in a simulation or with the robot in a safe mode first.
s6p: We work with your safety officer and supplier. In the EU, the Machinery Regulation and the AI Act apply to safety-related AI.
qP: Tell us which robots you use and what should get easier. You get a clear proposal by email. You pay nothing unless you agree.

q1: Which robots does this work with?
a1: Any robot or fleet that has a documented way to send commands or read status, for example through its vendor software, an API or ROS 2. For the help bot, manuals and service notes are enough.
q2: Do we need to change our robots?
a2: No hardware changes. The AI layer runs next to your existing software, and the robot's own safety settings stay as they are.
a3: We agree on that before we start. Manuals and logs can stay on your own servers, and we tell you exactly which AI service is used and what it receives.
q4: Is this connected to the $MAIGA coin?
a4: No. This is a normal service paid by invoice. No token, no crypto, nothing on-chain.
